metadata.title: A sharp auxiliary ratio for a three-point kernel argument and its conditional consequences for zeta zeros
metadata.description:
Correction: only the sharp ratio theorem is claimed. The kernel-level inequality uses two steps of Wang's preprint arXiv:2609.24167v1 (a Fourier identity and a ratio step), and the global proportions and the short-interval corollary use its whole framework. On 6 October 2026 its author replaced that preprint on arXiv by a notice that a new method is needed to obtain a good improvement, so all three are conditional and not claimed.

We prove that the auxiliary ratio in Wang's three-point kernel argument has sharp maximum sqrt(2), attained exactly at (0,1) and (1,0). Substituted into the source-pinned framework of arXiv:2609.24167v1, it would give a lower proportion 0.6725007995946757558... of nontrivial zeta zeros that are simple and on the critical line, with a distinct-zero companion 0.8362503997973378779.... Directed rational intervals and an independent 120-decimal interval replay certify the numerical comparisons. The result is asymptotic and does not prove the Riemann hypothesis.
metadata.version_notes: Correction: the kernel-level inequality is now stated as conditional on two steps taken from Wang's replaced preprint (his Fourier identity and his ratio step), which v0.02 claimed unconditionally; sentences presenting Wang's withdrawn result as established are reworded; the sharp ratio theorem is the only claim. Reproducibility facts added. Title changed accordingly.
